Commentary.Commentary: We're back. The Indian team is in a huddle near the boundary line with Hardik Pandya giving a pep talk. One question in everyone's mind - Will dew play a factor? Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka are the openers for Sri Lanka. Hardik Pandya to bowl the first over. Here we go...
... CHASE TIME ...

The Lankan bowling, as mentioned earlier, was brilliant. They kept a leash on India's scoring rate and by picking wickets at regular intervals, they didn't allow the home team to recover. That said, in the last 5 overs, they took the foot off the pedal a bit and India managed to score freely. A venue that is considered to be a graveyard for the bowlers, all the Sri Lankan bowlers apart from Kasun Rajitha fared exceedingly well and now the onus is on their batters to gain the series lead. Let's see how they approach the chase...

India started like a train on fire. They fetched 17 runs from the opening over and it appeared that we are in for a run feast at the Wankhede. However, the introduction of Maheesh Theekshana stifled India's charge in the Powerplay and they ended up with only 41 runs for the loss of two wickets. Thereafter Ishan Kishan and Hardik Pandya tried to gain some rhythm with their partnership but both fell soon to leave India reeling. It was the unbeaten partnership between Deepak Hooda and Axar Patel (68* off 35 balls) that allowed India to at least get a fighting total on the board.

A decent recovery from India in the end overs, fetching 61 runs off the last 5 overs - but it's still a below-par score at this venue. Sri Lanka will be very satisfied with the way they bowled, especially in the first half and will be backing themselves to chase it down under supportive conditions.

Well bowled! Kasun Rajitha comes from around the wicket for the final delivery and angles across a yorker around off. Deepak Hooda stays deep in his crease and plays it with an angled bat behind point for just a single. India finish with 162/5 on the board!
FOUR! Another delivery that is pitched up outside off, Deepak Hooda opens the face of the face and slices it over backward point for a boundary.
Swing and a miss! Another slower one, this time it's fuller and wider of the off pole. Deepak Hooda throws the kitchen sink at it but only connects with thin air. He lets out a huge cry of anguish.
SIX! Slower one gone wrong! This is pitched up right in the slot outside off. Deepak Hooda clears the front leg and dispatches it right back over the bowler's head for a biggie.
Fullish length on leg, Axar Patel drives it down to long on for a run.
Nicely bowled! This is full and quick, close to the off pole, Deepak Hooda manages to dig it out to covers for a single. 150 is also up for India.
FOUR! A boundary to end the over and 15 runs come off it. This is a half-volley outside off, Axar Patel frees his arms and lofts it over extra cover to pick up a boundary.
Full and wide, Axar Patel throws his hands at it and ends up slicing it over the point region for yet another brace. The 50-run stand is up between these two.

In the air...but lands safely! This is bowled into the pitch and around off. Axar Patel looks to loft it down the ground but mistimes it badly. The ball falls well in front of the fielder at long on and they race back for two.
Goes full and wide now, Axar Patel looks to thrash it away but is well beaten.
SIX! Wrong line! This is pitched up on the pads, Axar Patel uses the angle of the delivery and flicks it all the way over the backward square leg fence for a maximum.

Shout for an lbw, not given! A late call to take the DRS. Good-length delivery around leg and nipping back into the right-hander. Deepak Hooda looks to whip it away but misses. The ball goes off his pads and rolls toward backward point as they take a leg bye. There is half an appeal for lbw but the ball seems to be pitching outside the leg stump. Dasun Shanaka takes a late call for a review though. The UltraEdge is checked first and there's no bat involved. Ball Tracking shows that the ball is pitching in line but missing the stumps. The original decision stands.
Dilshan Madushanka is back into the attack as well to bowl the penultimate over.
Good length, on off and this is knocked down to long on for a single. A great comeback over from Kasun.
Slower delivery, on a length and well outside off. Deepak Hooda had already walked across his crease but leaves the ball alone. The umpire calls it a fair delivery and Hooda seems surprised.
Another slower one, very full and outside off, dipping on the batter. Axar Patel has to wait for it and he strokes it through extra cover for a single.
FOUR! A bit too predictable there Kasun Rajitha and Axar Patel finds his spot. This is on a length and around off, Axar holds his shape and jabs it back over the bowler's head for a boundary.

Well bowled! Goes full and outside off but it is an off-paced delivery. Axar Patel looks to thrash it through covers but is undone by the lack of pace and gets an inside edge that rolls to the keeper.
A length ball on middle and leg, Axar Patel looks to drive but ends up punching it back gently toward the bowler.
Kasun Rajitha returns to bowl at the death. 0 for 28 in his 2 overs so far.
SIX! Deepak Hooda is punishing anything short here. Quicker one at around 95 clicks but it is dragged down around middle. Hooda rocks back and muscles it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
This is full on middle and leg, Axar Patel sweeps it down to deep square leg for yet another single.
A touch of flight and bowled on middle, Axar Patel blocks it out.
A tad shorter and around leg, Deepak Hooda looks to heave it away but mistimes the ball through square leg for a single.
Floats it up now around off, Axar Patel leans forward and drives it down to long on for one more.
A googly to start off with. This is on the shorter side and on leg stump, Hooda goes on the back foot to flick it behind square leg for a single.
Change in bowling. Wanindu Hasaranga to bowl out now.

On a nagging length and pushed outside off, Hooda looks to work it off the back foot but gets an inside edge toward mid-wicket. They scamper through for the single. 17 off the over, a big one for India. Spoils the figures of Maheesh but still it's a good one, 4-0-29-1.
SIX! Two in a row! Looks to bowl it quicker and onto the pads, Deepak Hooda heaves it in between deep mid-wicket and long on for yet another maximum.
SIX! High and handsome! This is a half-tracker around middle, Deepak Hooda picks it up and launches it a long way over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Pushed through on off stump, Patel eases it off the back foot down to long off for one.
This is quicker and flatter at 100.6 clicks and on the pads. Axar Patel works it away in front of square on the leg side and picks up a couple of runs.
Maheesh Theekshana comes back on for his final over and starts with a shorter one around middle. Deepak Hooda whips it away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller again, around off and shaping in, Axar flicks it off the inner edge to wide long on and returns for the second run. 100 up for India!
Beaten all ends up! Full and close to off, shaping away late, Patel tries to drive but is beaten on the outside edge.
Wide! Short and around off, jumping extra off the surface, Axar allows it through. Wide called for height.
In the channel outside off, nipping away off a length, Patel allows it through to the keeper.
A 130 kph delivery, short and outside off, Patel tries to cut but misses.
EDGY FOUR! Full in length and around off, Axar tries to drive without any footwork and edges it down to third man for a boundary.
Axar Patel is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Dilshan Madushanka returns for another spell and removes the Indian skipper. Sharp delivery, short and on off, angling away. There isn't much room for the batter to play the cut shot but Pandya tries to force the issue off the back foot. He ends up edging it to the keeper. They appeal and the finger goes up after some delay. Hardik Pandya returns dejected and India are staring down the barrel with half the side back in the hut.
Commentary.Howout: c Kusal Mendis b Dilshan Madushanka

Commentary.Commentary: Dilshan Madushanka (2-0-14-0) is back into the attack.
Almost drags it on! A touch short and on off, Hooda hangs back to flick it across the line but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It deflects to backward point.
Loopy and full, around middle, Pandya drives it back past the diving bowler to long off. They cross.
Quicker and fuller on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Flighted this time, around middle, Hooda uses his feet and flicks it to deep mid-wicket for another run.
Identical to the last delivery, this time Pandya works it to deep mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
Shortish and on middle, helped on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
Wanindu Hasaranga (2-0-9-1) comes back in but from the opposite end.
Shortish and on middle, hit across the line to deep square leg for a single. 5 from the over and Maheesh continues to impress.

A corker of a yorker from Maheesh Theekshana. Around leg and sweeping the batter off his feet. Pandya attempts to dig it out but loses his balance as he goes down flat on the ground. Waqar Younis will be proud of this delivery!
Flattish and just outside off, Hooda walks forward and eases it past the diving bowler to long off. They cross.
Flatter one, full and on the pads, Pandya picks it off his pads and works it to deep square leg for one.
Quicker and on middle, it's forced down to long on for a single.
Miscued! Flighted and a bit short around leg, stopping off the surface, Pandya plays a mistimed lofted shot down to long on. They cross.
Maheesh Theekshana (2-0-7-1) is brought back into the attack.
Bowls it on a length and just outside off at 129.1 kph, Pandya drives it past the bowler to long on and takes a single.
Fuller on middle, angling in at 134.2 clicks, Hooda eases it down to long on for a single.
Slower one, on a shortish length outside off at 97.6 clicks, Pandya cuts it to deep point for a single.
Play and a miss! Pace up this time from Chamika. Shortish and around off, at 139.4 kph, Pandya stays back to pull but misses.

FOUR! The movement from the batter puts the bowler off. Chamika Karunaratne opts for the slower one but gets his line all wrong. Serves it down the leg side at 97.2 kph, and Pandya needs no second invitation to put it away past short fine leg.
Short in length, around off, Hooda goes back to pull but doesn't get hold of his shot. He mistimes it to deep mid-wicket and they take a single.
Chamika Karunaratne (2-0-14-1) is back into the attack.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it towards short mid-wicket.
Loopy and full, around off, Hooda flicks it a bit aerially and past mid-wicket. Once it goes past the fielder, they cross.

Appeal for stumping! Yet another googly, landing full around off and fooling the batter. Hooda is forward to drive but it spins back in to beat the inside edge. The keeper is quick to take the bails off and appeals. The square leg umpire refers it upstairs. The third umpire first checks for the inside edge which is absent. The side-on angle then shows that the back foot of Hooda is well grounded.
Deepak Hooda is the new man in.

OUT! Kishan holes out! A body blow to India as the set batter departs. Wanindu Hasaranga dishes out a well-disguised wrong 'un, landing full around leg at 92.5 kph and getting it to bounce a tad extra. Ishan Kishan kneels down to smoke it across the line but it flies from the higher part of his bat and Dhananjaya de Silva takes the skier safely at deep mid-wicket. India are reeling at the moment.
Commentary.Howout: c Dhananjaya de Silva b Wanindu Hasaranga

Commentary.Commentary: Yet another googly, full and on off, Pandya goes hard at it and inside-edges it down to fine leg. They cross.
Flighted googly, landing full around leg, Kishan sweeps against the spin and sends it behind square leg for a single.

Drinks break. India have shown little recovery after losing three wickets in quick time. Ishan Kishan has stuck around for a while now and holds the key. Hardik Pandya has joined him with positive intent and the hosts will be relying on this pair to prepare the launching pad for the end overs. Sri Lanka have done a great job thus far but they cannot rest on their laurels. In this format, the momentum changes in the blink of an eye. Let's see how the next phase pans out.
Length ball, slower in pace yet again and angling it in from around off. Hardik Pandya walks toward the ball and just defends it out.
This is bowled at just 104.7 clicks and around the top of off, Kishan drives it down to long off and turns the strike over.
Keeps bowling it slower, this is on a length and around middle and leg. Ishan Kishan eases it back to the bowler.
Another slower one but the length is pulled back a bit, Kishan nudges it in front of point.
FOUR! Slower one, in the slot around off, Ishan Kishan waits for it and just creams it through covers for another boundary.

SIX! Kasun Rajitha comes back into the attack hoping for a change in fortune but gets dismissed instead. This is full and wide outside off, Ishan Kishan throws his bat at it and slices it over the backward point fence for a maximum.
Kasun Rajitha is back on. He bowled the first over of this match and went for 17 runs. Can he redeem himself?
A touch fuller and on off, Hardik Pandya drives it straight to the man at extra cover.
This is flatter and bowls around off, Pandya pushes it toward the cover region.
Tosses it up a bit and bowls it full on off stump. Ishan Kishan looks for the slog but gets it off the inner half of the bat to deep mid-wicket for one more.
This one is pushed through at 87 clicks, Pandya drives it through mid off and collects a single.
Flatter one around off, Pandya punches it out towards extra cover.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Wanindu Hasaranga fails to pick up a wicket off his first delivery as it was struck at maximum speed by Hardik Pandya. This is a real drag down around off, Pandya goes deep in his crease and clobbers it right back at the bowler who gets a hand on it and yet the ball speeds away into the long on fence.
Will Wanindu Hasaranga come into the attack? Oh, yes! Here comes the mystery man.
Goes a bit fuller and angles it well across the left-hander. Ishan Kishan looks to open the face of the bat and guide it away but finds the man at backward point.
Shorter and around off, Pandya stays on the back foot and dabs it through backward point for a single.
Back of a length and over middle, Hardik Pandya punches this one in the gap between deep mid-wicket and long on for a couple of runs.
Misses out this time! Length again outside off, Hardik Pandya connects the cover drive sweetly yet again but finds the fielder inside the ring.

FOUR! And again, this time off the back foot! This is the leg cutter from Chamika Karunaratne, a tad shorter and around off. The ball stands up nicely and Hardik Pandya punches it well in front of cover for another boundary.
FOUR! Top shot! A length ball around off, Hardik Pandya plays a lovely high-elbow drive off the front foot and creams it through the cover region for a boundary.
Chamika Karunaratne to continue...
Flatter delivery on the pads, this is turned away in front of square leg for a single. Hardik is away!
Skipper Hardik Pandya is in next with India in a spot of bother.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust for India! Dhananjaya de Silva holds this one back a touch and bowls it at 86.6 clicks. This is a touch short and around off but once again the ball sticks on the surface. Sanju Samson stands his ground and doesn't move his feet as he looks for the big hoick across the line. The ball flies off the top edge and comes down around the short third man region where Dilshan Madushanka takes the catch. Spin is proving to be effective here and we haven't even seen Wanindu Hasaranga bowl yet.
Commentary.Howout: c Dilshan Madushanka b Dhananjaya de Silva

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker and shorter around off, this is played off the outer half of the bat and wide of the man at third man for a couple of more runs.

SAMSON IS SAFE! Good effort from Charith Asalanka but in vain. Dhananjaya de Silva comes from over the wicket and bowls it short around middle. Sanju Samson rocks back and pulls it aerially towards the deep mid-wicket fence. The timing isn't right and Asalanka is a bit slow to come in. Asalanka puts in the dive and grabs it with both hands but the replays show that the ball clearly touched the ground.

Is that a clean catch? Charith Asalanka is unsure. His teammates are celebrating. The two umpires get together and then refer it upstairs. The soft signal is not out. It's grassed and the crowd roars.
Drops it short now and on off, Ishan Kishan bends his back and pulls it down to long on. The fielder collects it on one bounce and they cross for a single.
Starts off with a tossed-up delivery from around the stumps. Ishan Kishan looks to use his feet but there is a hint of turn and he checks his shot to block it out.
The field restriction is not there anymore. Here comes Dhananjaya de Silva...
Good length around off, Ishan Kishan bunts it out on the off side for a quick single at mid off. Just 3 runs and a wicket off the over and at the end of the Powerplay, India are 41/2!

Nice change of pace. Ishan Kishan looks to come down the pitch, Chamika Karunaratne sees him coming and pulls back the length and bowls it under 115 clicks. The ball sticks in the wicket and Kishan does well to keep it down on the off side. Certainly got surprised.
Fullish length, angling in from around off, Sanju Samson drives it toward mid off and scampers through to get off the mark.
On a good length and angling into middle and leg, Samson strokes it away toward mid on.
Nicely timed but well stopped as well. This is pitched up around off, Sanju Samson plays a high-elbow cover drive but fails to beat the man at extra cover.
WIDE! Chamika looks to bowl full and attack the pads but spills it down the leg side for a wide.
Sanju Samson is the new batter, coming ahead of Hardik Pandya.

OUT! CAUGHT! Chamika Karunaratne strikes with his very first delivery and India lose their second wicket inside the Powerplay. This is bowled on a good length outside off stump and at 128.9 clicks. Suryakumar Yadav shuffles across, trying to get inside the line of the ball and scoop it over short fine leg. SKY gets himself into a bit of a tangle and the ball lobs up in the air off the toe end of the bat. The ball lands down around short fine leg where Bhanuka Rajapaksa takes a simple catch after his initial reaction to run behind. A big breakthrough for Sri Lanka and Dasun Shanaka is delighted. Perhaps the lack of pace brought his downfall.
Commentary.Howout: c Bhanuka Rajapaksa b Chamika Karunaratne

Commentary.Commentary: Chamika Karunaratne is into the attack to bowl the last over of the Powerplay.
Fullish and around off, skidding in, Kishan leans forward but plays a mistimed drive off the inner half. Another excellent over for Sri Lanka.
Flatter one, on middle, it's punched down to mid on where the fielder makes a partial stop with a dive. They cross.
Uses his feet to a full ball and pushes it down to wide long on for a single.
Quicker one on the pads, worked behind square leg for a single.

IN THE AIR... SAFE! Maheesh Theekshana darts it in, short and on middle, Suryakumar Yadav goes deep inside the crease to flick it on the leg side but fails to close the face of his bat in time. It flies towards mid on but lands safely in front of the fielder stationed there.
Flatter and shorter on middle, skidding in, Kishan gets back and hits it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, angling away at 135.3 clicks, Yadav flicks it off the inner half to short mid-wicket. A good couple of overs for Sri Lanka.
A touch short and outside off, at 139.3 kph, Yadav forces it off the back foot but finds the cover fielder on this occasion.

FOUR! Timing and placement of the highest order. Back of a length, around off, Suryakumar Yadav eases himself on the back foot and punches it sweetly through the gap between extra cover and mid off. Wow, just wow!
Play and a miss! Short in length and wide outside off, at 136,2 kph, Suryakumar Yadav goes chasing after it as he attempts to cut but misses.
Fuller in length, around middle and off at 136 kph, SKY shuffles across a bit and defends it on the leg side.

Almost drags it in. Dilshan Madushanka lands it on a good length, around off and nipping in at 137.8 kph, Kishan tries to defend near his body but it takes the inner edge. The ball beats the stumps by a whisker and rolls wide of short fine leg. They cross.
Fuller and on middle, Kishan eases it down towards wide long on for a run.
Flatter and around off, skidding into the left-hander, Kishan is on the front foot as he defends on the leg side.
Turning down the leg side, Yadav clips it towards deep square leg and opens his account with a single.
Suryakumar Yadav walks in at number 3.

OUT! GIVEN LBW! Maheesh Theekshana delivers it a bit short around off, skidding in and hurrying the batter. Shubman Gill goes on the back foot to pull but misses and is rapped on the back thigh pad. They appeal and the finger goes up. Shubman Gill has a word with his partner and takes the referral. A flat line as the ball passes the bat, shows the UltraEdge. Time for the Ball Tracking and it shows that everything is in line. Three reds and Gill returns cheaply.
Quicker one, full and around leg, Kishan helps it through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted delivery, full and around off, Kishan tries to drive but the bottom hand comes off and he mistimes it back to the bowler.
An immediate change in the bowling as Maheesh Theekshana comes in to replace Kasun Rajitha.
Shortish and on leg, Kishan taps it down to square leg and picks up a single. 9 from the over, it's been a good confident start from India.
On a length and around off, Ishan forces it through the line but finds mid off.
Aerial but wide of the fielder. Fractionally short and around off, angling away, Gill pushes inside the line and it flies off the outer half. Goes wide of backward point and they get a run.
Pitches it up and around off, at 139.1 kph and shaping back in, Gill flicks it off the inner half and it races in front of square on the leg side. They get two runs.
Too full and around off, shaping in a touch, Gill goes hard at it and it comes off the inside half of his bat. Rolls back to the bowler who stops it with a dive.
FOUR! A glorious way to open your account in this format. Fullish and outside off, Shubman Gill leans into the drive and caresses it past the diving cover fielder for a boundary.
Wide! Wrong start from Dilshan Madushanka. The left-arm pacer serves it full and very wide outside off, at 137 clicks, Gill is not chasing it.
Dilshan Madushanka to steam in from the other end.

FOUR! It's a colossal first over, 17 from it! Short in length, around off and angling in, Kishan swivels on the back foot and pulls it thunderously to the deep backward square leg fence. The crowd is loving it!

FOUR! Well played in the end. Kasun Rajitha comes from 'round the wicket and decides to bowl the slower one. It turns out to be a full toss and Ishan goes with the shot despite getting deceived. He has to reach out but still finds the sweet spot as the ball races behind the bowler for a boundary.
Fuller and straighter, Ishan flicks but finds the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Wide! Kasun is struggling with his line. Slips a length ball way down the leg side, Kishan tries to wrist it away but misses.
SIX! Ishan Kishan is in the mood already! Kasun Rajitha delivers another one close to the pads, full in length, Ishan picks it up and dumps it with disdain over deep square leg for a maximum.
Pitches it up and around middle, some movement there, Kishan pushes it down to mid on.

India are away! Rajitha begins with a full ball around leg, Kishan works it off his pads and eases it in front of square on the leg side. They collect a couple of runs and Ishan is off the mark as well.

Done with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the play underway. The two umpires are already out in the middle and the Lankan players also stride out to take their places on the field. Ishan Kishan will open the batting alongside Shubman Gill for India. Kasun Rajitha has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the play. But first, the two sides walk out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems as it is the first game of the series. It will be Sri Lanka's national anthem first followed by the Indian national anthem.

Ishan Kishan comes up for a quick chat! He starts by saying it's difficult to switch formats (was playing red-ball cricket recently) but it's important to do that at this level. Adds that he has played a lot of games here at the Wankhede and is aware of how the pitch behaves. Mentions that he just looks to watch the ball and play on merit. Tells that he is excited to play this series. States that he was very worried after Pant's accident and hopes that he recovers soon and returns.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Kusal Mendis (WK), Pathum Nissanka, Dhananjaya de Silva, Charith Asalanka, Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Dasun Shanaka (C), Wanindu Hasaranga, Chamika Karunaratne, Maheesh Theekshana, Kasun Rajitha and Dilshan Madushanka.

India (Playing XI) - Shubman Gill (On T20I debut), Ishan Kishan, Suryakumar Yadav, Hardik Pandya (C), Sanju Samson (WK), Deepak Hooda, Axar Patel, Harshal Patel, Shivam Mavi (On debut), Umran Malik and Yuzvendra Chahal.

Hardik Pandya, captaining India for the first time in this format at home, says that he is excited to lead the country and it is a special moment as well. Adds that they were going to bat first even though it is a chasing ground as they want to challenge themselves. Mentions that anyone who plays for the national team is the best and they have two debutants, Shivam Mavi and Shubman Gill. Mavi comes in the side to replace Arshdeep Singh who isn't available.

Dasun Shanaka, the captain of Sri Lanka, says that they want to bowl first as dew could be a factor later on. Adds that they have been doing well in this format, except for the T20 World Cup and they will look to follow the routine. Informs that they have retained the same batting unit and there are a few changes in the bowling group with Kasun Rajitha and Maheesh Theekshana back in the mix.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and Dasun Shanaka calls it correctly. Sri Lanka opt to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta is pitchside. He says that the dimensions of the ground aren't big and the pitch looks good. Ajit Agarkar joins him and says that there's a true covering of grass and it will have an even bounce that will help the batters even further. Adds that there might be dew later on and it is going to be a tough night for the bowlers.

Given that it is the year in which the ODI World Cup is to be held, a T20I series might seem pointless but it also serves as a good opportunity to try out new players and keep the core players of the ODI side fresh by giving them a rest. With that said, there are a couple of big news coming from the Indian camp - Firstly, a fit-again Jasprit Bumrah has been added to the Indian roster for the ODI series against Sri Lanka which takes place after the T20I series. The second big update is that Shivam Mavi and Shubman Gill both will be making their T20I debuts in this game.

Sri Lanka have a few familiar faces returning to the T20I setup but there are some who have left out as well. Dasun Shanaka will once again lead the side in both the T20I and the ODI series and will be hoping for a change in fortune as he looks to beat the mighty Indian team at their home. It won't be easy but Sri Lanka are the reigning Asia Cup champions and have match-winners like Wanindu Hasaranga, Bhanuka Rajapaksa and Pathum Nissanka on their side. The conditions will prove to be useful for the visitors as well and with the recent success of the 2022 Lanka Premier League behind them, the Lankans can notch up more than just an upset. So, will the touring side start off with a win? Or will India show why they are the top-ranked side in the world? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

India have a new-look T20I side for this series with Hardik Pandya leading the contingent and Suryakumar Yadav acting as his deputy. A lot of new faces, especially in the pace department have been added and also the likes of Ruturaj Gaikwad, Rahul Tripathi, Sanju Samson and Shubman Gill will look to impress the selectors and consolidate their place in the national setup. It remains to be seen whether all of these new faces get a chance to show their worth but with recent criticism of the white-ball side, it is a must-win series for the hosts in order to re-establish their status as one of the best T20I sides in the world.

Hello and a warm welcome ladies and gentlemen to the coverage of the 1st T20I between India and Sri Lanka at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. It is a brand new year, the year of the ODI World Cup and it is a brand new bilateral white-ball series between the two sub-continental nations. The Lankans have never won a bilateral T20I series in India and with a fairly young Indian side drafted for the series, the visitors have the best opportunity to change that stat. However, India's depth in this form of the game is unmatched and with home conditions behind them, the hosts will be up for the challenge.
... MATCH DAY ...

Yet another action-packed year of cricket has flown by and it is now time for a new series to begin as India welcome Sri Lanka for a three-game T20I and a three-game ODI series. The T20I series is up first and the opening match of the series will take place at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. The hosts, India have been playing away from home for quite a while now but will begin 2023 with a home series and look to do well. As for the visitors, Sri Lanka, they haven't played international cricket since the end of November but most of their players will be fresh after a decent break and will be well-prepared as well due to the Lanka Premier League. The hosts have a new look to their side with Hardik Pandya being appointed as captain of the T20I series yet again. The likes of Ruturaj Gaikwad and Ishan Kishan are mostly likely to feature as the opening pair for India. Umran Malik and Washington Sundar who also featured against New Zealand and Bangladesh in recent times have been given an extended go in the T20I series and it will be Arshdeep Singh who will lead the bowling for the hosts. There have been a couple of surprise additions to the pace armory as well with Shivam Mavi and Mukesh Kumar being called up for the T20I series. Sri Lanka have made a few changes from their last series against Afghanistan back in late November 2022. The likes of Dinesh Chandimal and Asitha Fernando have been left out even after good performances in the LPL. Dasun Shanaka will captain the side in both series and for the T20I series, it will be their star, Wanindu Hasaranga who will act as Shanka's deputy. Sri Lanka have also recalled Chamika Karunaratne and Avishka Fernando who was the top-scorer in LPL 2022. Another addition is that of Nuwan Thushara for the T20I series and one might say that he has completely deserved it. The visitors are the reigning Asia Cup champions but they couldn't transform the same form in the T20 World Cup and will need to play at their best at all times to snatch a win off the hosts who have been dominant in bilateral T20I series at home in the past year or so. India are a team that is going through a bit of change with senior players being rested or being used for just one format of the game and they will try to form a base for the side that can take them into the next T20 World Cup in 2024. With both sides looking to start off the new year with a win, it is the hosts who have a stranglehold when it comes to recent bilateral series between these two nations. Will India continue to show their dominance in bilateral T20I series at home? Or will their sub-continental counterparts rise up to the challenge and start off with a win? We shall find out.
